sections.h2: Where does Caldwell County record a deed?
sections.html:
Deeds for property in Caldwell County are recorded at the Register of Deeds office at 905 West Avenue NW in Lenoir. The office is open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, and its notices show it closes with the rest of county government on holidays such as Veterans Day.

The office has held real estate records since 1841, the year the county was formed. Its own site describes the job as keeping the permanent record for deeds, deeds of trust, mortgage cancellations, powers of attorney and maps. Wills are a different filing: the office's FAQ says they go to the Caldwell County Clerk of Court, not to the register of deeds.

If you plan to sell a Caldwell County house, the recorded deed is the document that moves ownership on the public record. North Carolina gives priority to whichever competing document was recorded first, and the county office tells owners to record as soon as a deed is signed. Read the recording priority statute if you want the exact wording.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Caldwell County?
sections.html:
Recording a standard deed costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for every page after that, and a deed of trust costs $64.00 for the first 35 pages. These are uniform statewide fees set in G.S. 161-10, so Caldwell County charges the same schedule as every other county.

ItemAmount as printedSource
General instrument, such as a deed$26.00 for 15 pages, then $4.00 per extra pageG.S. 161-10
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for 35 pages, then $4.00 per extra pageG.S. 161-10
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo feeG.S. 161-10
Nonstandard document add-on$25.00G.S. 161-10
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added pageG.S. 161-10
Deed excise tax$1.00 per $500.00 of consideration, which the county office also words as $2.00 per $1,000.00G.S. 105-228.30 and the Caldwell County FAQ

The statute calls the fee schedule complete and exclusive and says it is collected before filing. Ask the office what payment types it accepts before you go, since that detail is not on the pages the county publishes online.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax on a Caldwell County sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays it. The Caldwell County FAQ says the tax of $1.00 per $500.00 of the purchase price is paid by the grantor at the time of recording, and G.S. 105-228.30 puts the duty on the transferor and requires payment to the register of deeds before the instrument is recorded.

  • The tax applies to each instrument that conveys an interest in real property.
  • Half of the receipts stay in the county general fund and half go to the state, under the same statute.
  • In a typical closing the settlement agent collects the stamp amount from the seller's proceeds and pays it when the deed is filed.
  • If the deed is a gift with no consideration, ask the office how it treats the instrument before you sign.

When you sell to a cash buyer, the same rule applies. The price on the contract drives the stamp amount, so confirm the number with the closing attorney before the deed is drawn.

sections.h2: What does a deed need before the Caldwell County office will record it?
sections.html:
The office lists three requirements on its real estate page. Every deed needs the current mailing address of the grantee, every deed and deed of trust prepared in North Carolina must name the draftsman on the front page, and a document to be mailed back needs a postage paid, pre-addressed envelope.

The office scans each document when it is presented and hands it back or puts it in the outgoing mail, so there is no waiting period for a return. North Carolina also has recording standards adopted in 2002, and the office links them from the same page. One summary of those standards, published by the Carteret County office on the coast, asks for a 3 inch blank top margin on the first page, type of at least 10 points, one-sided pages and the instrument type stated at the top.

Staff cannot fill in forms or run a title search, because the office page says state law bars the unauthorized practice of law. Its FAQ confirms that you can write your own deed but recommends an attorney, and says a name can only be added to or removed from a deed by recording a new deed.

sections.h2: How do I search Caldwell County land records before I sell?
sections.html:
You can search them online from the register of deeds site. The county says every real estate index since the formation of the county is online, and images of the documents are online from the early 1900s forward.

Use that search to pull the vesting deed, any deed of trust that has not been cancelled, and any easement or road maintenance agreement on your parcel. The office page names road maintenance agreements as a record type it holds, so check for one if your driveway is shared. A lost deed is not a crisis: the office issues a certified copy under its seal.

  • Look for an open deed of trust and ask the lender for a payoff letter.
  • Check that every owner named on the deed is signing the sale.
  • Look for recorded agreements that run with the land.

All records in the office are public, with narrow exceptions for certified vital records and military discharges under 80 years old. Veterans can record a DD214 there at no charge, and the county uses that recording for its Thank-a-Veteran discount card.

sections.h2: How does the Caldwell County tax bill affect a closing?
sections.html:
The county tax bill is owed whether or not the house sells, and unpaid tax is a lien on the parcel that has to be settled at closing. The Tax Office is at the same Lenoir address, open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the county's tax site gives 828-757-1340 as the office phone.

That office says it keeps records on all real and personal property in the county, runs six departments, and also bills the rescue readiness charge, 14 fire districts and three municipalities: the Town of Sawmills, the Town of Rhodhiss and the Village of Cedar Rock. Its notice says bills go out in July with a 2% discount for July payment and 1% for August, taxes are due September 1, and payment without interest runs through January 5.

Under G.S. 105-360, interest is 2% from January 6 and three-fourths of one percent a month from February 1. Caldwell County went through a general reappraisal for 2025; its commissioners were told in February 2025 that the county's sales ratio had fallen below the 0.85 threshold in state law, and the appraisal was done by county staff for residential property. Ask the Tax Office for your parcel's current value and any rate adopted since.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Caldwell County?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 81,105 residents on July 1, 2025, up 0.5% from the 2020 base, and counts 38,057 housing units. Land area is 471.89 square miles, which works out to 170.9 people per square mile in 2020.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home, 2020-2024: $192,200.
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 73.5%.
  • Median gross rent: $744.
  • Median household income: $56,425.

Those figures come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for Caldwell County. About 22.8% of residents are 65 or older. Older owners with modest income can ask the Tax Office about the state's elderly and disabled exclusion, which is the greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value, with an income limit of $38,800 for the 2026 tax year.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed in Caldwell County without an attorney?
faqs.a: Yes, the register of deeds office says you can make your own deed, but it recommends an attorney because staff cannot give legal advice or check title. The deed still has to meet the recording requirements, including the grantee's mailing address and the draftsman's name on page one.

faqs.q: What are the hours of the Caldwell County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, at 905 West Avenue NW in Lenoir. Marriage license applications stop at 4:30 p.m. so staff can finish the last one before closing.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when I sell a house in Caldwell County?
faqs.a: The seller does. The county FAQ states the tax is $1.00 per $500.00 of the purchase price, paid by the grantor when the deed is recorded, and the state statute names the transferor as the payer.

faqs.q: Does the Caldwell County register of deeds keep wills?
faqs.a: No. The county's FAQ says wills are filed with the Caldwell County Clerk of Court. If you are selling an inherited house, ask the clerk about the estate file and the register of deeds only about the deed history.

faqs.q: How far back do Caldwell County land records go?
faqs.a: The office holds real estate records back to 1841. Its online search covers every real estate index since the county was formed, and document images are online from the early 1900s onward.
